records.subject: Demand for recognising Assemese script in ISO - 15924 and ISO/IEC-10646
records.SM_Text:
Shri Pabitra Margherita: In the August Parliament, I already appealed for recognizing Assamese as a classical language and subsequently Assam Publication Board. Asom Sahitya Sabha and Government of Assam are already working on it. Now I would like to appeal for taking necessary steps to recognize Assamese script in ISO 15924-2004 and ISO/IEC 10646. The origin of the Assamese script can be traced back to the early decades of the fourth century. But unfortunately, in ISO and UNICODE documents and code chart, Assamese script has not been appropriately recognised. Earlier Assamese script was recognised by DIT (Meity) and C-DAC. In ISCII, the code for Assamese script was 57006. (ISCII) was the standard recognized by Government of India for the Indic scripts before Unicode standard was accepted. Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is one of the recognizing authorities of script code for Indian Languages. According to documentary evidence, BIS encoded Assamese script independently for Assamese language in 1991. But in ISO/IEC 10646, which provides a code for the representation of names of scripts, Assamese script is missing. Similarly, in ISO/IEC 10646, which is related to Unicode, Assamese script is not recognized properly. I earnestly appeal for recognisation of Assamese script in ISO and Unicode. BIS has the authority to forward the demand to ISO for recognising and encoding the Assamese script in its standards. Therefore, I request the concerned Government authorities to take the necessary steps to ensure the recognisation of Assamese script in the National and International standards, thereby preserving the heritage.

?(Ends)

records.subject: Demand to declare ostomy patients as specially abled i.e. “Divyang”
Demand to declare Assamese language as a classical language of India.
records.SM_Text:
SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA (Assam):Thank you, Vice-Chairman Sir. With your permission, I would like to speak in Assamese. I also thank this august House for having the facility of Assamese to English interpretation.

My subject pertains to an appeal to declare Assamese language as a classical language of India. *"Among the languages included in the larger Indo-European linguistic family, Assamese is an ancient language that is recognized by the Indian Constitution and spoken by about 23 million people.

Multiple States in the North-Eastern India have been using Assamese as the lingua franca. This language has continuous history of about 2,000 years. Along with the development of the language, examples of literary work in Assamese have been found since the eighty-ninth century BC. The most important aspect is Ramayana was translated into Assamese language ? the first translation of the epic in any language in the Northern part of India ? way back in 14th century by Madhav Kandali. Considering the glorious history of the language and its literature, Assamese is eligible for being recognized as a classical Indian language alongside the six already-recognized classical languages because Assamese language fulfils all the criteria required for this recognition. Under the leadership of hon. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, academic measures have already been initiated for this. Therefore, I appeal for steps from the Central Government to recognize Assamese as a classical language."

(Ends)
